The Petitioner has approached this Court for a direction to the Respondents for grant of compensation for a sum of Rs.50 lakhs for harassment and delayed justice to the family of the deceased.
2. The facts of the case reveal that an accident happened on 15.04.2005 where the mother of the Petitioner herein lost her life.
The facts further reveal that an RTI application was filed by the Petitioner only on 27.08.2020 inquiring about the status of the case.
There is a complete silence on the part of the Petitioner from 2005 to 2020 regarding the claim which arises out of the death of the mother of the Petitioner.

A reply was given on 22.09.2020 to the RTI application filed by the Petitioner stating that the file is pending with the office of the SDM (Dwarka) and that the application is being This is a digitally signed order.

3. Material on record also discloses that the SDM (Dwarka) on 03.10.2020 wrote a letter to PIO,
Sector-23, Dwarka stating that the RTI application does not pertain to this office.

sentences.text:
The grievance of the Petitioner is that he is entitled to compensation and because of inaction on the part of the Delhi Police in proceeding further under Section 166 (4) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
which provides that an accident report should be treated as an application for compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
The Petitioner was denied the compensation which was payable on account of the death of the mother of the Petitioner.

5. The short question, therefore, arises for consideration before this Court is whether the failure of the Police to transfer the accident action report to the Tribunal would entitle the Petitioner for compensation for a sum of Rs.50 lakhs, as claimed by the Petitioner.

6. Mr. Satyakam, learned ASC for GNCTD, draws attention of this Court to an Order dated 05.11.2009 passed by this Court in FAO 842/2003 wherein this Court has taken steps to streamline the application of compensations where accident action report has not been forwarded to the Tribunal by the Police.

Paragraph No.4 of the said Order dated 05.11.2009 reads as under:
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 20:33:23 4.
The Delhi Police has started compliance of Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act w.e.f. 8th June, 2009 after the order of this Court.
However, there has been no compliance during the period 14th November 1994 up to 7th June, 2009 which has caused grave prejudice to the victims of the road accident.

Many of the victims of the road accidents during the period 1994-2009 have filed the cases before the Claims Tribunals which have already been decided and no action is required in respect of those cases.
There is second category of victims of the road accidents who being ignorant of their rights have not filed the claim petitions before the Claims Tribunals.
It is very difficult to trace out such victims and no action is proposed in respect of the second category of cases at this stage.

There is third category of cases where the victims of the road accidents during the period 1994- 2009 have filed cases before the Claims Tribunals but the cases are pending for services of the owner, driver and/or eye-witnesses and non-production of relevant documents.

This Court is of the opinion that Delhi Police should effect the service of summons on unserved owner, driver and eye-witnesses, produce the relevant documents and also file report under Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in such pending cases.

The Delhi Police is, therefore, directed to carry out the following actions relating to the pending cases:-

sentences.text: (i) The Delhi Police shall file Accident Information Reports under Section 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in respect of all the pending cases filed before the Claims Tribunals after 14th November, 1994.
(ii) The Delhi Police shall collect the list of all pending cases filed after 14th November, 1994 from the Claim Tribunals and shall file the

(iii) The service of summons on the driver, owner and eye-witness in all pending cases, if not effected, shall be effected through the Delhi Police who shall ensure their service and production before the concerned Claims Tribunal.

(iv) The Delhi Police shall also place on record the relevant documents before the Claims Tribunal including FIR, MLC/post mortem report, site plan, driving licence, registration cover, Insurance policy, fitness, permit, etc. at the time of hearing of the cases before the Claims Tribunal.
(v) The Delhi Police has already deputed a Naib Court with every Claims Tribunal.

The Naib Court shall remain present at the time of hearing of all the cases and the Claims Tribunal shall pass the appropriate order for filing of the report under Section 158(6), service of the owner, driver and eye-witness or production of documents as the case may be.

The copy of such orders shall be given dasti to Naib Court whereupon the Naib Court shall note down the next date of hearing of the cases,
coordinate with the concerned Police Stations and provide the status report of those cases to the Court on the next date of hearing.
The compliance of this order shall be done by Delhi Police in a phased manner.

(vi) In the event of non-compliance of this order by Delhi Police, the concerned Tribunal shall bring the same to the notice of the ACP concerned in the monthly meeting between Claims Tribunals This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 20:33:24 and the ACsP in terms of order dated 8th June, 2009."
(emphasis supplied)

7. A perusal of the aforesaid paragraph reveals that upto 7th June, 2009 there has been no compliance of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act which has caused grave prejudice to the victims of road accidents between the year 1994 and 2009.
The fact is that the Delhi Police has not been active in complying with the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act from the year 1994 to 2009.

sentences.text: Even though, the Petitioner, who is an advocate, has not taken any steps as mandated under law and has in fact started agitating his rights only after 15 years of the death of his mother, this case is being considered on its facts, as an exception.

Therefore, in facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court is inclined to apply the principles of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 for granting compensation to the Petitioner.
9.

The relevant portion of Section 4 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 reads as under:-
"4. Amount of compensation.--(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the amount of compensation shall be as follows, namely:--
(a) where death results from the injury an amount equal to [fifty per cent.] of the monthly wages of the deceased [employee] multiplied by the relevant factor;
or an amount of [one lakh and twenty thousand rupees], whichever is more;"
This is a digitally signed order.

The GNCTD is directed to pay an amount of Rs.1,25,000/- to the Petitioner being the son of the victim as an extraordinary measure on the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case.
11. In light of the aforesaid, the writ petition is disposed of, along with pending application(s), if any.

12. Needless to state that it is always open for the Petitioner to make an application before the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal (MACT) on the basis of available records and the Tribunal is requested to consider the case in accordance with law.
SUBRAMONIUM PRASAD, J SEPTEMBER 14, 2023 S. Zakir/Ur
